title: Cost, Speed, and Scale: Caching, Batches, and Limits

questions.prompt: Order how a request is rendered for prompt caching.
questions.explanation: Requests render as tools, then system, then messages. Caching is a prefix match, so stable content should come first.

questions.prompt: Cache reads stay at zero across identical requests. What's a likely cause?

options.text: A timestamp or other changing value early in the system prompt

questions.explanation: Any byte change in the prefix invalidates the cache. Move volatile content after the last breakpoint, or remove it.

questions.prompt: The Message Batches API processes requests asynchronously at ____% of standard prices.
questions.explanation: Batches are 50% off. Most finish within an hour, with a 24-hour maximum.

questions.prompt: Which levers save money without reducing quality? Select all that apply.

options.text: Always switching to the smallest model

questions.explanation: Caching, input hygiene, and batching are free wins. Smaller models and lower effort are trade-offs you should measure first.

questions.prompt: Match each usage field to what it reports.

pairs.right: Tokens written to the cache this request

questions.explanation: These fields show whether caching works and where your spend goes. Thinking is billed as output.

questions.prompt: Why should you match batch results by custom_id?

options.text: Results can arrive in any order
Position-based matching is required by the API

questions.explanation: Batch results aren't guaranteed to be in request order, so key them by the custom_id you assigned.
